paid_market_gaps.gap: Version-banner ASV findings flag backported-patched Apache/PHP/OpenSSH; merchants must manually dispute false positives each scan
Low-cost ASV packages sell scans and SAQs, not remediation; merchants still fix or dispute findings themselves
Enterprise FIM (Tripwire) is quote-only; cheaper OSSEC alternatives market against its premium price
Merchants paying processor PCI fees still do SAQ work themselves; fees don't ensure compliance

wtp_evidence: Merchants pay small amounts: ASV scans $81.90/year (Sectigo HackerGuardian via reseller) to $185/year (Clone Systems, 1 target), processor PCI fees ~$120/year, non-compliance fees ~$20-$30+/month push validation; buyers treat it as a junk-fee chore, and hosted payment pages shrink scope.
bundling_note: Processors bundle scans/SAQs, hosted checkouts (Stripe) cut server scope, hosts sell add-ons, Wazuh gives free PCI FIM, and AWS Security Hub/Defender Plan 2 include PCI checks/FIM.
summary: Crowded, commoditized market of cheap ASV scans and FIM, bundled by processors, hosts and clouds. Thin opening: automated backport-aware false-positive dispute and remediation for hosts/MSPs serving self-hosted PHP merchants; low ACV.
